stem: A 16-year-old presents after a risky bicycle stunt and says he knew it would probably be fine; which developmental feature best explains this behaviour?

options.text: Adolescents are mainly injured because they are difficult for drivers to see
Adolescents are protected by better judgement than younger children
Adolescents make poor risk assessments and may feel invincible
Adolescents have the lowest exposure to injury because they are closely supervised
Adolescents are less likely to take risks because peer influence is minimal

explanation: Adolescents make poor risk assessments and may feel invincible. This developmental pattern helps explain why some teenagers underestimate danger and engage in risky behaviours.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Adolescent injury risk is strongly influenced by developmental judgement and a sense of invulnerability.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because difficulty being seen by drivers is a visibility issue more relevant to younger children, not the main developmental feature described here.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adolescents do not generally have better judgement than younger children in this context; risk assessment is often immature.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because adolescents commonly underestimate risk and may feel invincible, which fits the behaviour described.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because adolescents are not characterised by the lowest injury exposure due to close supervision.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because peer influence is often significant in adolescence, and this option contradicts the risk-taking pattern in the stem.
